newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Purim a day etched in Israeli memory.
newsitem.headline: Purim a day etched in Israeli memory.

text.p: The Jewish festival of Purim has in recent years been marred or marked by events etched in the memories of Israel's Jews.

The holiday, which begins in Tel Aviv this year on Saturday night, is a day of joy marking the salvation of Jews from genocide in ancient Persia. Here are some events that have occurred recently on Purim, which is set by the Jewish lunar calendar.
- 1991: The Gulf War ends. Iraqi President Saddam Hussein stops firing Scud missiles after lobbing 39 of them at the Jewish state.
- 1992: A Palestinian mistaken for a costumed Jewish reveller stabs to death a young woman and a man in Jaffa, near Tel Aviv, and wounds 19 people, most of them children.
- 1994: Jewish settler Baruch Goldstein slaughters 29 Palestinians at Hebron's Cave of the Patriarchs before survivors strangle him to death.
- 1996: Islamic militant suicide bomber blows himself up, killing 13 people in Tel Aviv on the eve of Purim.
- 1997: Suicide bomber kills himself and two other people at a Tel Aviv cafe.
